messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

What matters is a fair financial share for each of us. I haven’t agreed to subsidize A’s discounted purchase, and I’m not signing off on it as things stand. B should have a fair chance to benefit too, though I can’t decide what she wants. I want the house and will handled clearly and fairly; I’d like it settled, but there’s no real rush. “Fairness” and “clarity” fit my needs.

For me, the need is well-being; financial independence matters to that. Buying the house with my husband at a family discount is one way I hope to support it, but I know C hasn’t agreed, and nothing about price or shares is settled. I also want a fair, clear process for all three of us, and to understand what B needs money for. No other discomfort comes to mind.

I suppose having some room to shape my own future matters to me; a dance studio is the way I can see doing that. I don’t know what amount or share would be fair. I’d also like the house decisions and any price or discount discussed clearly, though I don’t have a settled view on who should buy it.

#2: Yes—“a genuine choice about any agreement” fits. I haven’t agreed, and I don’t want pressure to substitute for my choice. #5: Not quite; I’d say “time to reach a considered resolution, without artificial urgency.” Fairness means a fair financial share for each of us, not me subsidizing A’s discount. B should have a fair chance to benefit too. Clarity means transparent terms and a clear process. Both still fit. I’m not holding back.

#6 fits: well-being, especially financial security and independence, matters to me because I want to be able to support myself. #7 fits; I want each of us to agree freely, not feel pressured. #8 fits; fairness and clarity would help us make informed decisions. #9 fits; understanding each sister’s needs matters for that. “Well-being” alone feels broad. No other discomfort comes to mind.

Yes, #10 fits; it matters to me to have choices about my future. I’m happy to leave the studio out of the NCE, though it’s the practical reason I’m hoping for money. #11 fits too: I’d like a fair amount to help start it, but I don’t know what’s fair. #12, clarity, fits because I want to understand the house and financial terms. #13 fits; I’d like space to decide without pressure, and I still don’t have a buyer preference. No other concern comes to mind.

Yes, “time to reach a considered resolution, without artificial urgency” fits. I want this settled, but not rushed; a considered decision matters more than an invented deadline. I have no other discomfort to add.
Yes, “financial security and independence” fits. They matter because I want to be able to support myself and have choices. No discomfort with the process comes to mind.
Thanks. The wording for my concerns looks right to me; I don’t have another concern or discomfort to add just now.
